text: People are genuinely just shitting on this song, and honestly, it's a bit disappointing because part of me did not like this song at first, but when I listened to it again, I realized how well thought-out this was. He didn't just make this song chaotic, fast-paced, and overstimulating for no reason. The song is literally about the cyclical nature of things like war and violence, as well as religion, and I don't think he could've portrayed it any better. These are heavy subjects, and the fast-paced, chaotic, overstimulating nature reminds me a lot of how social media and the way the internet is; it's very overwhelming and it makes it hard to digest, JUST LIKE THE SUBJECT MATTER. I think people are just crapping on this song without thinking about why he made certain vocal and lyrical choices or why it's paced the way it is. I actually love this song, and mind you, I do not listen to FIR regularly. This song only came up because I was really hyperfixating on listening to Slipknot, and I was looking up his features to listen to other songs with him in it, and this came up. I remember laughing a bit about the content and thought it was a little ridiculous, but obviously my opinion's changed. I hope more people take the time to actually analyze the lyrics and how this is framed to understand the song, because I really do think they put a lot of thought into it. It honestly took a bit for me to admit my opinion changed because I feel embarrassed that I just laughed because I was taking it at face value for the visuals and the chaos. Anyways, I really love this song, and I also wanna add that Radke is extremely skilled, and the amount of range he has is INSANE!! I am just astonished at the skill. As a big metalhead, I LOVE the screams, growls, and gutturals SO much. Also, I really leaned into the chaotic nature, and it's now become a part of my gym playlist lmao. Oh, and as a former choir person and someone who sung a lot when I was younger, his singing voice is also great! I did learn that he used a real choir as well, and the little choir me is so happy about that lol hell yeah! Genuinely sick asf!!!

5- escape the fate callout right before the breakdown.

6- the drums and guitar work during Serj's solo are from 2 different parts of chop suey.

I can't explain enough how cool this song is to me. First off I loved the first album of etf when Ronnie was in it. Second I love serj from soad so freaking much and everything he does.  And Corey was amazing when I saw slipknot in like 2011. But the obvious aside. I love how Corey is actually in his mask, and when he says "you cannot escape your fate" and then serj comes in with his beautiful lyrics that are always so deep. And how he hits the run on "enough". Also when he says "them" right before the little mini break down gets me because I feel like it's his signature note (to me anyways). And I really feel like he wrote the part that says "repeat the cycle" because it gives such a soad vibe. And then when him and Ronnie harmonize on "enough" I got chills. 
And the breakdown at 3:14 is nasty. Then of course the video is just sick AF. 
I haven't been this excited about a new song in I can't even remember how long. It just gives me such a big rush of nostalgia. I literally teared up when I heard it ❤️🥹

Involvement in killing and prison sentence

On May 6, 2006, at approximately 2:30PM, Radke met with Marcel Colquitt in Las Vegas, Nevada at the north end of Decatur Boulevard near Shadow Ridge High School to fight.[34][35] Each man brought additional men to support them in the fight. During the fight, 22-year-old Chase Rader, a man who had accompanied Radke, shot 18-year-old Michael Allen Cook, killing him, as well as wounding another man, Colquitt's brother.[36] Radke was arrested for and charged with murder but the district attorney declined to prosecute him, despite his confession, as it was determined Radke acted in self-defense.[36][37][38][39]

Radke pleaded guilty to battery with substantial bodily harm and to owning and bringing brass knuckles to the brawl (illegal in Nevada); subsequently, he was placed on probation for five years and ordered to pay $92,372 in restitution to Ceda Freeman, Cook's mother.[35][40][41] After Radke violated the terms of his probation, he was sentenced to serve two and a half years in prison.[42][43][35]

Because of his prison sentence, Escape the Fate fired Radke. Craig Mabbitt, formerly of the band Blessthefall, replaced the imprisoned Radke.[44][10]
Domestic violence arrest

On May 1, 2012, Radke was accused of striking his then-girlfriend, Sally Watts, and was subsequently arrested in Glendale, California, on August 6, 2012, after he had failed to make an appearance at any of the scheduled court hearings.[45][46] He was officially charged with a misdemeanor count of corporal injury and misdemeanor false imprisonment by the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department.[47] He was released on $30,000 bail. On May 14, 2014, Radke pleaded no contest to disturbance of the peace.[48][49]
Six Flags assault arrest

On September 29, 2012, Radke was performing as part of Falling in Reverse for FestEVIL, a metal festival for Six Flags Great Adventure's Fright Fest event, when he threw three microphone stands into the audience at the close of a performance, injuring a 16-year-old girl, who was taken to the hospital, and a 24-year-old man, who was treated at the scene.[50] Radke was charged with simple assault and aggravated assault and released on $25,000 bail.[51][52] Radke publicly apologized for his actions, saying that his actions were not in anger and that he had not intended to hurt anyone.[53][6] Six Flags subsequently decided to ban hard rock and heavy metal bands from performing at the park in the future.[54]

In the years following, he has since claimed that he never apologized for the incident and does not plan to because it "helped [his] persona", stating "I'll fucking do it again."[55][56]
Rape allegation and defamation lawsuit

On June 10, 2015, it was reported that Radke had been publicly accused of sexual assault by a 25-year-old woman. The accuser alleged that Radke had sexually assaulted her after Falling in Reverse's performance at the Murray Theater on June 3, 2015. Though it was determined that Radke had contact with the woman, police found no evidence that Radke or his entourage had assaulted the woman.[57] Radke subsequently filed a lawsuit for defamation.[58][59]
Anthony Fantano defamation lawsuit

In August 2024, Radke filed a defamation lawsuit against online music critic Anthony Fantano.[60] In the lawsuit, Radke accused Fantano of defaming him in a video titled "This Guy Sucks", as well as a since-deleted tweet where Monuments' frontman Andy Cizek referred to Radke as the "Bill Cosby of alt music".[61] The case was later dismissed under the anti-SLAPP statute in Fantano's favor with Radke ordered to pay Fantano's legal fees.[62]

text:
I’m really torn about how I feel about this song. I love Falling in Reverse, and Ronnie is talented as hell. The videoclip alone speaks for itself—it felt like watching a mini movie, and honestly, better than most movies I’ve seen lately.
That said, I feel like the song itself is messy and unfinished. Then, out of nowhere, it seemingly turns into a Slipknot song—which I personally struggle with because I can’t stand Corey Taylor. His part completely ruins the flow for me.
Then it suddenly feels like it turns into a System of a Down song, and THAT part I absolutely love. It genuinely made me feel like my 15-year-old self came back for a moment! 😂
So overall, I have very mixed feelings about this one. There are parts I absolutely love, but as a whole, I definitely don’t think it’s one of Ronnie’s best songs.

text:
Hello. I’m a devout a proud Falling In Reverse hater, but I thought to myself that I’d give this song a shot, so here’s my honest take on this song.
Honestly, I really liked some of the instrumental parts, if it weren’t for the overproduction of the whole song, which I don’t have room to say, because it’s basically apart of every band these days. The breakdown at the end was cool too. Ronnie Radke’s lyrics were corny for the most part, and I feel the whole “I don’t wanna go to heaven, I wanna burn in hell” type of lyrics just make you look like you wanna be edgy, while coming out looking like a complete idiot. I don’t think the dude has a bad range, just the lyrics are cringe, and the opera vocals he does are just hilarious. Corey’s vocals I liked, but that’s biased since I’m already a huge Slipknot fan. I feel bad to say that this is probably one of the worst vocal performances Serj Tankian has ever done. Listen to any SOAD album, and his vocals are awesome. Here, however, they’re just stale. I did kinda dig the acoustic part where he comes in, especially the lyrics, because the dude’s Shakespeare at writing political and anti-war songs. Anyways, in summary, I’ll give it maybe a 3 stars out of 5 if I’m feeling generous. The song was mediocre at best if I’m being honest, but not as bad as I thought it would be. Overall hilarious as hell. Good job Ronnie, you impressed me, somewhat

text:
If you map out the songs in this chaotic, high-as-fuck way:

Last Resort (Cover): "Am I gonna make it?" This is rock bottom and the most fragile state.

I'm Not a Vampire (the elevator ringtone version): "I got demons inside me, or am I actually the problem myself?"

Popular Monster: The world turned me into a monster.

Voices in My Head: Where’s the real enemy? This is where the line blurs—what others say about us becomes the static in our own heads.

Zombified: Or are you guys the ones getting brainwashed? Shifting the issue from the individual up to a societal level.

Watch the World Burn: Watching the world collapse from both the character’s internal pain and society’s decay. It’s the turning point from "victim" to "rebel"—though not quite a world-destroyer just yet.

Ronald (Ronnie's actual first name): "This is who I am." Becoming an uncontrollable entity. Picking Alex Terrible and Tech N9ne feels like slamming two distinct languages of violence head-on into each other.

God Is a Weapon: Marilyn Manson actually has a co-writer credit on this. Humans inserting violence into systems of belief, sex, and power. Manson’s whole career has been about dragging religion, taboos, authority, morals, sex, and societal norms into the light to challenge them.

Joseph: Takes its title from his middle name—his full name being Ronald Joseph Radke. Realizing that rage, pain, religion, power, and violence can all be weaponized to build a endless loop. And the two voices Ronnie chose to witness this track are:

Corey Taylor: Pure human rage and agony.

Serj Tankian: Questioning war, power, and genocide.

This whole thing is literally the ultimate "Ronnie Radke Character Arc"—and it’s nowhere near over based on how that MV ended. I fucking can’t wait for the next drop!🤘🤘🤘

text:
“Joseph” is, above all, a piece of musical art to me, and art doesn’t always have to make perfect sense. It can be chaotic, excessive, emotional, and suddenly turn into something completely different. Not everything has to be rational or fit neatly into one genre or a traditional song structure.

Different styles, completely different voices, hard transitions, and moments where you genuinely have no idea what’s coming next. And that’s exactly what makes it so interesting. At some point, you stop trying to analyze the song and just let it take you wherever it wants to go.

And somewhere along the way, it made me think of “Bohemian Rhapsody.” Not because “Joseph” is a copy or even sounds like it, but because of that same sense of musical freedom. Queen brought completely different worlds together in rock and pop without caring whether they fit into a conventional song structure. To me, Ronnie is doing something similar here with the language of modern hardcore and metal, but entirely in his own way.

And somehow, in a time filled with so much uncertainty, this song feels strangely fitting. It’s restless, contradictory and emotional. It actually does something to you instead of simply playing in the background.

My conclusion: this is definitely a song I want to experience live. Not just hear it. Experience it.

text:
Sharing, if it can help someone else:

Songs like this one can be quite instrumental in addressing childhood traumas in the St. Francis of Assisi kind of sense: Forgiveness as a means of releasing the burdens off of our backs so that we may travel light. (Reconciliation is a different matter.)

It’s okay to completely let go of someone who harmed you beyond repair. Forgiveness doesn't have to mean letting them back into your life; sometimes, the healthiest way to love someone who abused you is from an unreachable distance, wishing them well from afar.

For me, one of those persons was my birth mother, LaQuita. 

I recall telling my multi-talented, beautiful partner that morning that it would have been another decade before I would dare ever reaching out to her ever again, as we parked in front of a quaint vitamin shop. My stare drawing blank, upon picking up my phone, as I was made next of kin to handle her affairs back in April 2024. 

I made the trip with a sliver of hope that I might find some childhood photos (Spoilers: None were found).

.... No one told me that suicide was the cause of death until morning of visiting her apartment. Suicide letter stacked on boxes of Bibles .... Worst week of my life punctuated by some the worst food poisoning experienced from seafood tacos. (As an aside, I recently enjoyed a tasty ahi tuna taco. Fear officially obliterated.) ....

Some days still feel raw. Those are the days to be most gentle with myself and others. I’ve been using mantras like "not knowing is most intimate," which has helped me find peace with the "why" that I will never know. Instead, I choose to keep my eyes forward (skill issue), focusing on the beauty in my life. Every breath is a new chance for reflection, forgiveness, and gratitude.

There is a real freedom in being unashamed of a "f'd up" origin story. 

Back to the song that bears my namesake, it would be pretty cool to have laser eyes and lightning powers. And having Serj Tankian and Corey Taylor on the track? Wow.

Travel lightly with love

как на острие беспощадно насажен.

и волос немытый ладонью приглажен.

подгнивший, помятый которые сутки,
худой аксакал среди прочих домов,
промокший почти что до пор штукатурки.

Весь город, хранящий в себе этот дом,
под льющими струями сверху.
В нём хата - монетка в фонтане большом
с запасом монет, означающим веху.

Звучанья сырой непогоды снуют,
легко беспокоят натяжки всех веток,
родителей, что вечно ищут уют,
увы, неспособных к рождению деток.

Внутри потаённый груз старых обид,
как камень, как топит нырнувшего в реку,
как бремя, которым по нёбо я сыт.
Он тянет ко дну, как иных тянет в Мекку.

Шумит за оконцами, звери точь-в-точь.
А я, как окурок утопленный в чае,
живу эту сильно дождливую ночь,
которую буйная буря венчает.

text:
En mi opinión, Joseph me decepcionó bastante. Con Corey Taylor, Serj Tankian y Ronnie Radke esperaba algo mucho mejor, porque los tres tienen estilos y voces muy reconocibles.

No soy artista ni músico profesional ni nada por el estilo; solamente soy un oyente que decidió dar su opinión. Tampoco soy una persona que acostumbre criticar a los demás, pero esta vez sinceramente quise decir lo que pienso. Sé que mi opinión puede estar bien o puede estar mal, y entiendo perfectamente que a los artistas probablemente les dé igual lo que yo piense, porque simplemente soy un oyente más.

Siento que la canción intenta combinar demasiadas cosas y termina sobrecargándose. La parte de Ronnie, para mí, está demasiado explotada; la voz melódica de Serj no me terminó de convencer y siento que tiene un toque demasiado cinematográfico. Corey sí me llamó la atención al principio, pero después la combinación con la guitarra acústica tampoco terminó de funcionar para mí.

No digo que los artistas sean malos. Todo lo contrario: precisamente porque son artistas reconocidos y esperaba mucho de ellos, sentí que pudieron haber trabajado mejor la combinación de sus estilos en este tema, en lugar de sobrecargarlo.

Para mí, tener fama o ser reconocido no significa automáticamente que una colaboración vaya a funcionar. Si tienes la oportunidad de juntar a artistas de este nivel, yo esperaba algo que realmente aprovechara sus estilos y que sonara mejor integrado.

Esta es solamente mi opinión como oyente. No pretendo decirles a los artistas cómo hacer música ni creer que mi opinión es la verdad absoluta. Simplemente esto fue lo que sentí al escuchar la canción completa por mi cuenta.

I'm so confused with how I feel about this. For one, I didn't expect this collab ever, let alone in 2026. 

I was shockingly impressed with Corey's presence in this song. Serj's voice has been better on other tracks, but that's only to be expected given his age, definitely added polarity to the track. The breakdown was actually by far the most impressive part of this song, for sure. 

I don't understand @1:24 at all... My ears and brain reject that this part was needed, or even remotely appreciated. I don't know if it's a genre/style I don't like, but I've definitely heard and appreciated other artists doing this. I just think this was far too far out of Ronnie's wheelhouse to even attempt, but who am I to judge. As far as a listener goes, I definitely disliked it.

Additionally, the cinemaphotography constantly focused around Ronnie's presence, his "ipso-facto self-indulgent" aura, I found to be incredibly douchey. No other way I could say that, unfortunately. Either you understand my point, or you have no idea what I'm going on about. 

The subject of the song, though? Fucking FIRE. An absolute gold mine in 2026, where the lyrics describe current events in an artistically accurate and phenomenal way. Incredible work on that, for sure, wouldn't change an iota of it.

text:
I know this probably won’t be a popular opinion, but I genuinely believe that a lot of the hatred surrounding this collaboration on “Joseph” is misplaced. 
Before judging the song solely because of who is involved, did people actually read the lyrics—or even listen to the song? I can imagine that some refused to do so because of the controversy surrounding the collaboration, but that’s precisely what makes the discussion interesting. 
What caught my attention is that the song directly addresses something Serj Tankian has been criticized for: the perception that he no longer follows or stands by the convictions and principles he has spoken about throughout his career. Whether you agree with that criticism or not, the lyrics clearly engage with that subject. Personally, I was immediately curious to hear what they had to say, and I absolutely loved the result. 
Of course, people are going to criticize the music video and Ronnie Radke because of the controversy surrounding him. That’s fair. But playing devil’s advocate for a moment, there’s an old saying that comes to mind: “Talk about it, good or bad—but talk about it.” 
And ultimately, that’s what art can do. The message in the lyrics doesn’t disappear simply because people dislike the person delivering it. If anything, the controversy may push more people to actually hear the words and think about what the song is saying. 
I’m not saying everyone has to like the collaboration, the video, or even the song itself. But I do think “Joseph” deserves to be judged as a piece of music and writing, rather than dismissed solely because of the people involved. 
Personally, I think what we got is a genuinely interesting and powerful project—and, in my opinion, it deserves far more credit than it’s been getting.
No matter what many will say, it's a masterpiece. 🔥 The lyrics won me over and I won't let them go. I might even listen to them on repeat 🤯🖤

text:
I honestly don’t understand how this ended up being the final version. Having Corey Taylor and Serj Tankian on the same track sounds incredible on paper, and that’s exactly why this is so disappointing. You have two extremely recognizable and powerful vocalists, yet the song never feels like it takes full advantage of what they can actually bring to the table.

The biggest problem for me is that the whole track feels strangely underwhelming. It starts with a lot of potential, but instead of building into something genuinely impactful, it just kind of stays there. The songwriting feels predictable, the instrumental lacks the kind of punch I was expecting, and the production seems to prioritize making everything sound polished over giving the song any real character.

And honestly, I was expecting much more from the vocal collaboration. Corey and Serj have completely different voices and styles, which could have made for an absolutely insane combination. But rather than creating an interesting contrast between them, it feels like their appearances were added because their names look impressive together on the credits. I kept waiting for that moment where everything would click, but it never really happened.

The clip itself doesn’t help either. Visually, it feels like it’s trying to look dramatic and epic without actually having much to say. There are plenty of big shots and serious faces, but very little that feels memorable or visually distinctive. Considering the people involved and the expectations surrounding this release, I really thought the video would have a stronger identity.

Maybe I’m being too harsh, but when you put Corey Taylor and Serj Tankian together, you naturally expect something special. This feels more like a missed opportunity than an actual collaboration that needed to happen. There’s nothing here that makes me want to come back and listen to it again, and that’s probably the biggest issue for me.

I’m glad people are enjoying it, but personally, this is nowhere near what I expected from a track with these two names attached to it. It could have been something genuinely memorable, and instead it just feels… forgettable.

text:
How does anybody take this bullshit seriously? He doing the same thirst trap pose from God is a Woman on top of all the usual narcissistic song and dance. Genuinely a bit upsetting that these kinds of artists get so much support from people who buy their image and branding despite it being so paper thin and superficial. Performative activist and male final boss, though with his background I do understand why this stuff manifests like it does. Not completely understand, could probably never, all I can see is the art itself and what it evokes or doesn't evoke in me. Dont get me wrong, many parts of the song sound great, obviously everything is well polished and technically sound but really I just have to ask "What's the point of this if it's meant to be art?" 

Corey I understand being on something like this, he's creatively bankrupt. But Serj? Genuinely sad to see. Such a great guy, I'd hope he could see more of how gross this whole scene is. Whoever keeps letting Ronald stroke his ego with these videos like a 14 year old making themselves the *super cool edgy tatted OP antihero protagonist* it's just a bit lame. Genuinely upsetting seeing shit like this get solid production and talented musicians involved, wasteful.
